hero.headline: Murkowski opposes Blanche for attorney general, threatening confirmation
hero.body:
Sen. Lisa Murkowski announced Friday she will vote against Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general, putting his confirmation in serious jeopardy. The Alaska Republican becomes the second GOP senator to publicly oppose the nominee, joining Sen. Susan Collins of Maine.

Murkowski said in a Friday morning post on social media that the country needs an attorney general who will check the worst impulses of the administration. She stated she lacks confidence that Blanche would fulfill that role if confirmed.

The opposition from both senators is significant because Republicans control the Senate with only a narrow margin. Blanche can afford to lose just two Republican votes, assuming all Democrats vote against him and Sen. Mitch McConnell remains absent. With Murkowski and Collins both opposed, the nomination faces substantial obstacles.

Louisiana Sen. Bill Cassidy remains undecided on the nomination, adding uncertainty to Blanche's path forward.

However, the source material indicates that Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, who were previously holding out on their support, announced they would advance Blanche's nomination after reaching what they called a "successful negotiation of a legally enforceable document." This agreement addressed concerns about provisions in a Trump settlement with the Internal Revenue Service.

Specifically, the document formally ends a planned 1.8 billion dollar fund referred to as an "anti-weaponization fund." The agreement also clarifies that Trump and his family will not receive indefinite protection from audits of future tax filings. Both the fund and the scope of Trump's immunity from audits had become dealbreakers for Cornyn and Tillis.

"We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund," Cornyn and Tillis said in a joint statement. They added that the department acknowledged in a binding written order that the audit settlement is limited to the plaintiffs in the original lawsuit and does not extend to other parties.

The attorney general position oversees the Justice Department and serves as the nation's chief law enforcement officer. The role includes supervising federal prosecutors and providing legal counsel to the executive branch.

Blanche, who is already serving as acting attorney general, is scheduled to face a Senate judiciary committee vote on his permanent confirmation.

The Senate judiciary committee is due to vote on whether to approve the nomination and send it to the wider Senate for a vote. The timing of the vote had not yet been scheduled at the time the original article was written, though the source material indicates it would occur soon after the agreement was reached.

cards.headline: Trump Imposes 15% Tariff on Polysilicon for Solar Panels and Microchips
cards.teaser: The administration announced new tariffs on polysilicon, a critical material used in solar panel and semiconductor manufacturing, as part of trade actions targeting China.
cards.body:
Donald Trump has ordered a 15% tariff on imported polysilicon products, effective December 4. Polysilicon is a critical ingredient in microchip manufacturing and solar panel production, with China dominating global supply. The administration aims to strengthen US chip and solar panel supply chains to compete with Beijing in artificial intelligence and energy sectors.

The tariff targets Chinese polysilicon producers as part of broader efforts to reduce American reliance on Chinese supply chains for strategic materials. Solar industry stocks responded positively to the announcement, viewing the measure as protective of domestic manufacturing interests.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Pays $1.2 Billion to German Energy Firm to Cancel Offshore Wind Leases
cards.body:
The Trump administration has agreed to pay German energy company RWE $1.2 billion to terminate offshore wind project leases. This deal represents the latest action in a broader pattern of canceling renewable energy initiatives that the administration has long opposed.

RWE, one of Europe's largest energy companies, held leases for offshore wind development along the U.S. coast. The buyout comes as part of the administration's strategy to reverse renewable energy infrastructure that previous administrations had supported as part of climate and energy policy. The $1.2 billion payment to RWE marks one of several major settlements aimed at exiting wind energy projects.

Similar agreements have been reached with other offshore wind developers in recent months. One comparable deal involved $1.22 billion to cancel projects planned for California waters. These payments bring the total cost of offshore wind project cancellations to approximately $4 billion, according to multiple reports.

Offshore wind projects had been positioned as a central component of American renewable energy strategy. Federal leases were granted to multiple companies for development along both the Atlantic and Pacific coasts. Industry groups had projected these projects would create thousands of jobs and contribute significantly to carbon emission reduction targets. The cancellations represent a reversal of those plans and raise questions about the future of renewable energy development on federal waters.

The administration has long expressed skepticism about large-scale wind power and has indicated it plans to prioritize traditional energy sources instead. Officials have framed these cancellation payments as necessary to redirect energy policy away from what they view as inefficient renewable investments.

The specific federal budget allocation for the $1.2 billion RWE payment has not been detailed. Energy analysts have noted that the cumulative $4 billion in cancellation costs now exceeds the initial federal investment in lease sales and development support for these projects combined. This raises questions about the financial implications of reversing course on infrastructure that had already received significant public commitment.

The RWE agreement fits within a broader pattern of the Trump administration terminating clean energy initiatives. Federal officials have acknowledged scrapping more than $7.5 billion in federal grants for clean energy projects to states, with court filings suggesting these terminations were selective based on political considerations. The administration previously defended similar actions as protecting taxpayer dollars from waste.

These decisions represent a significant departure from the renewable energy direction established during previous administrations. The cumulative impact of project cancellations and grant terminations signals a fundamental shift in federal energy policy toward traditional power sources and away from the renewable infrastructure development that had been promoted as crucial for meeting national climate goals.

cards.headline: US Accelerates Military Partnership With Colombia to Combat Drug Trafficking
cards.teaser: Plans to target drug traffickers with American military assistance are underway as Colombia's new president takes office.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has fast-tracked a military partnership with Colombia aimed at targeting drug trafficking networks. The initiative is moving forward as Colombia's new president, who received endorsement from former President Trump, takes office. The partnership will involve U.S. military assistance and cooperation in operations against drug traffickers operating in Colombia.

Sweeping plans for the collaboration are already being implemented. Colombia has historically been a major source of cocaine production and a key partner for the United States in counter-narcotics efforts in South America. The accelerated timeline suggests both governments view the drug trade as an urgent priority requiring immediate joint action.

cards.headline: Rubio intensifies economic pressure on Cuba
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is conducting what he describes as an unprecedented economic campaign against Cuba's communist government.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters the administration is waging an economic war on Cuba and plans to increase pressure on the island's leaders. Rubio said the strategy aims to eliminate any relief mechanisms for the Cuban government.

Cuba's economy faces strain from U.S. sanctions and internal management issues. President Trump has not ruled out military action against the island nation, which is located 90 miles from U.S. shores. The economic pressure campaign represents an escalation in U.S. policy toward its longtime adversary.

cards.headline: States implement uneven protections against AI election deepfakes
cards.teaser: Twenty-nine states have laws addressing AI-generated election content, creating varied protections across the country ahead of the midterms.
cards.body:
Twenty-nine states have enacted laws governing AI deepfakes in elections, while California and Hawaii have had their laws blocked by courts. The patchwork of regulations means voters will experience different levels of protection from AI-generated political content heading into Election Day.

AI-generated attack ads and campaign materials have become widespread in the current midterm cycle, with candidates across the political spectrum using the technology. The lack of uniform federal standards leaves regulation to individual states, resulting in inconsistent protections for voters nationwide.

cards.headline: July Jobs Report Expected to Show Nearly 100,000 Positions Added
cards.teaser: The monthly employment report is anticipated to reveal steady but modest job growth, with analysts forecasting the economy added close to 100,000 jobs in July.
cards.body:
The Labor Department is releasing July employment data, with economists projecting roughly 100,000 new jobs were added during the month. The report is closely watched by investors evaluating labor market strength and potential Federal Reserve policy shifts.

Job growth is expected to remain modest compared to previous years, reflecting a cooling labor market from post-pandemic peaks. Young workers and unemployed job seekers are facing greater challenges in securing positions. Stock futures rose ahead of the report's release as markets awaited confirmation of employment trends.

hero.headline: Student Kills Seven in Shooting Rampage at Thai School
hero.body:
A 14-year-old student killed his grandparents at their home before opening fire at his school near Bangkok, fatally shooting five people on campus and then taking his own life, according to Thai police. The attack left eight people dead in total, including the teenage gunman, and wounded 22 others.

The shooting occurred on Friday morning at a high school on the outskirts of Bangkok. The teenager first killed his grandparents at their residence before traveling to the school, where he opened fire on students and staff members. Police arrived at both crime scenes to find multiple casualties. Nine people were reported to be in critical condition, according to Thailand's health department.

The incident represents a significant tragedy in Thailand, where school shootings remain relatively uncommon. The attack has raised urgent concerns about gun violence in the country and prompted immediate questions about how the teenager obtained the firearm and what may have motivated the violence.

Emergency responders worked to secure both the residential location and school campus while providing medical assistance to survivors. The school was evacuated and families were directed to designated safe locations to collect their children. Thai police established perimeters around both crime scenes as investigators began collecting evidence and interviewing witnesses.

One student who experienced the shooting firsthand described the harrowing experience. According to BBC News reports, a female pupil said she was standing in front of her teacher when the educator was shot. The student had to climb over a school fence to escape the violence.

The tragedy has prompted discussions about school security protocols and firearm access regulations in Thailand. Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the sequence of events and establish whether there were any warning signs that could have been detected before the violence occurred.

The shooting comes as Thailand grapples with broader questions about gun violence. While crimes involving firearms are more prevalent in some neighboring countries due to issues like unlicensed weapons proliferation, school shootings have been rare enough in Thailand to shock the local community deeply.

Police initially interviewed witnesses and the suspects in custody, though details about the weapon used and the identities of the victims have not been fully released by officials. As the investigation continues, authorities are working to piece together what led to the attack and whether the teenager had experienced bullying or other grievances that may have contributed to the violence.

The incident has raised alarm among parents and educators about student safety and the mental health challenges facing young people in Thailand's schools.

cards.headline: Activists Allege Abuse After Israeli Forces Seized Gaza-Bound Ship
cards.teaser: More than 20 people intercepted while attempting to break an Israeli blockade described beatings and electric shocks in custody.
cards.body:
More than 20 activists who attempted to break an Israeli naval blockade to reach Gaza said they experienced beatings, electric shocks, and other forms of abuse after being captured by Israeli forces. The activists were intercepted while trying to deliver aid or reach the territory by sea. Israel has maintained a blockade on Gaza, controlling access by sea and land.

Israel denied the accusations of mistreatment. The activists provided detailed accounts in interviews describing their treatment while in Israeli custody. The allegations add to ongoing tensions surrounding access to Gaza and the treatment of individuals attempting to breach the blockade. International humanitarian groups have long criticized restrictions on movement and goods into Gaza.

cards.headline: US Accelerates Military Partnership With Colombia to Combat Drug Trafficking
cards.teaser: Plans to target drug traffickers with American military assistance are underway as Colombia's new president takes office.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has fast-tracked a military partnership with Colombia aimed at targeting drug trafficking networks. The initiative is moving forward as Colombia's new president, who received endorsement from former President Trump, takes office. The partnership will involve U.S. military assistance and cooperation in operations against drug traffickers operating in Colombia.

Sweeping plans for the collaboration are already being implemented. Colombia has historically been a major source of cocaine production and a key partner for the United States in counter-narcotics efforts in South America. The accelerated timeline suggests both governments view the drug trade as an urgent priority requiring immediate joint action.

cards.headline: Iran's Nuclear Program Continues Despite Recent Conflict
cards.teaser: Officials and experts say military strikes may have slowed but not halted Iran's nuclear development activities.
cards.body:
Iran's nuclear program has continued operating despite recent military conflict, according to officials and nuclear experts monitoring the country's three key nuclear sites. While the pace of development may have slowed during the conflict, the program has not stopped. International observers have maintained focus on Iran's nuclear capabilities and the status of enrichment activities.

The assessment suggests that damage or disruptions from military action did not achieve a complete halt to nuclear operations. Iran has maintained nuclear facilities at multiple locations, each serving different functions in the country's atomic program. The continued operation raises questions about the effectiveness of military pressure in curbing nuclear development and the next steps in international efforts to address Iran's nuclear ambitions.

cards.headline: Investigation Examines Russian Links to German Airport Drone Bomb
cards.teaser: Evidence from previous cases suggests Russian-linked proxies handled drones and explosives and delivered them to Germany.
cards.body:
The BBC has reviewed evidence from previous cases showing that Russian-linked proxy groups have both handled drones and explosives and delivered them into Germany. German authorities are investigating whether Russia may be involved in a recent drone bomb incident at a German airport.

Investigators are examining connections between this incident and similar cases that involved comparable methods and materials, working to trace the device's origin and identify those responsible for placing it at the airport.

cards.headline: Meta Fined $567 Million in Child Safety Case
cards.teaser: The penalty is part of the largest child safety ruling against a social media company, bringing Meta's total fines to nearly $1 billion.
cards.body:
Meta has been ordered to pay $567 million in a New Mexico child safety case, the largest such ruling against a social media company. Combined with a previous $375 million penalty in the same case, Meta now faces nearly $1 billion in total fines. A Santa Fe district court found that Meta's platforms constitute a "public nuisance" and are a "significant contributing cause" of teen mental health issues.

The ruling reflects intensifying regulatory scrutiny of social media companies' responsibilities toward young users. Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, and other platforms used by millions of children and teenagers globally. Regulators are increasingly focused on how these companies moderate content, verify ages, and prevent harmful interactions involving minors.

cards.headline: American Evacuated From Antarctica in Midwinter Rescue
cards.teaser: An Australian flight crew battled subfreezing temperatures and near-constant darkness to evacuate a U.S. national to New Zealand.
cards.body:
An Australian aviation crew successfully evacuated an American from McMurdo Station during an extremely rare midwinter rescue operation. The team landed their aircraft in total darkness and temperatures of negative 43 degrees Celsius to retrieve the patient.

The patient was then flown to a New Zealand hospital for treatment. Midwinter evacuations from Antarctica are exceptionally uncommon because the severe conditions and near-total darkness make flight operations extraordinarily dangerous. This mission required specialized coordination to safely complete the rescue.

hero.headline: Meta fined $567 million in child safety case
hero.body:
A New Mexico court has ordered Meta to pay an additional $567 million in a landmark child safety lawsuit, bringing the total financial penalty to $942 million. The ruling concluded that Meta's platforms constitute a public nuisance that significantly contributes to harm affecting teenagers.

The case was brought by New Mexico's attorney general, Raúl Torrez, and represents the first jury trial to hold Meta liable for the actions and content on its platforms. A jury initially found the company liable in March, ordering $375 million in civil penalties after determining Meta had misled consumers about platform safety and enabled harms including child sexual exploitation. The second phase of the trial, which concluded with the additional $567 million judgment, was a bench trial focused on what reforms Meta should be required to implement.

The lawsuit was filed in December 2023, following a Guardian investigation that documented how Facebook and Instagram had become marketplaces for child sex trafficking. That investigation was cited multiple times in the original complaint.

New Mexico's attorney general's office has proposed several court-ordered reforms to protect children on Meta's platforms. These include implementing effective age verification systems to prevent adults from posing as minors, ensuring all teenage users receive appropriate safety protections, and enforcing minimum age requirements. The state also seeks safer recommendation algorithms that prioritize child wellbeing over engagement metrics, prominent warning labels about platform risks, permanent bans for adults engaged in child exploitation, and restrictions on end-to-end encryption for minors to prevent predators from operating covertly.

The reforms would be overseen and enforced by an independent court-appointed child safety monitor. Attorney General Torrez stated his office is exploring qualified independent technical monitors from across the country to fill this role.

Meta has strongly resisted these requirements, arguing they are technologically and practically infeasible. In court filings, the company threatened it would have no choice but to withdraw Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp from New Mexico entirely rather than comply with what it called "onerous" mandates. Meta argued that building separate versions of Teen Accounts for New Mexico would be excessively costly and challenging.

Torrez dismissed Meta's withdrawal threat as a "PR stunt," pointing out that the company has repeatedly modified its products and adapted to demands from various governments to maintain market access. He argued that Meta possesses the capability to implement these changes but refuses to prioritize child safety over engagement and advertising revenue.

A Meta spokesperson countered that focusing enforcement on a single platform represents a misguided strategy that ignores the hundreds of other apps teenagers use daily. The company also contended that requiring these changes infringes on parental rights and free expression for all New Mexicans.

cards.headline: Prediction markets allow bets on clinical trial outcomes
cards.teaser: Kalshi and Polymarket are offering markets that let people bet on whether clinical trials will succeed or fail.
cards.body:
Researchers have criticized prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket for allowing bets on clinical trial outcomes, describing the practice as "ghastly." Their main concern is that wagering on trials could create opportunities for insider trading and disrupt the drug development process.

The platforms defend their offerings, arguing they serve patients by providing valuable market-based information. According to Kalshi and Polymarket, these betting markets help people make better-informed decisions about medical treatments by consolidating public knowledge about trial prospects.

cards.headline: Firefighter deaths strain wildfire response workforce
cards.teaser: Deaths and close calls among wildland firefighters have raised questions about policies during an intense fire season.
cards.body:
Deaths and near-fatal incidents while fighting wildfires have placed additional strain on an already stressed workforce of wildland firefighters. When tragedy strikes, firefighters across the country check to see if the victim was someone they knew, reflecting the tight-knit nature of the profession.

The incidents have prompted questions about current policies and priorities as the country experiences an intense wildfire season. The workforce was already dealing with high levels of stress before the recent fatalities and close calls added to concerns about safety protocols.

cards.headline: Trump-backed Tennessee congressman loses primary
cards.teaser: Republican Representative Andy Ogles was defeated by a GOP challenger in the Tennessee primary.
cards.body:
Representative Andy Ogles, who had backing from former President Trump, lost his Republican primary race in Tennessee. The incumbent congressman was ousted by a challenger within his own party.

Ogles, who had been described as anti-Muslim in some coverage, faced opposition despite Trump's endorsement. The loss marks a setback for the former president's influence in certain congressional races, though Trump-backed candidates have won other primaries.

cards.headline: Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed discusses primary win
cards.teaser: Abdul El-Sayed spoke about his victory and the path forward after winning the Democratic primary in Michigan.
cards.body:
Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Democratic Senate primary in a competitive race against representative Haley Stevens. Commentators have characterized his victory as significant, with some arguing it offers a template for how Democrats can respond to Trump's political challenge.

El-Sayed ran on progressive positions and has discussed his primary win in interviews covering topics including his relationship with Senate leadership and his family. Analysts suggest his candidacy may energize Michigan Democrats heading into the general election, while his Republican opponent is attempting to appeal to Democratic voters by capitalizing on divisions from the primary.

cards.headline: Norway federation calls for FIFA president to resign
cards.teaser: The Norwegian Football Federation wants Gianni Infantino to step down over attempts to sell World Cup stakes.
cards.body:
The Norwegian Football Federation has called for FIFA President Gianni Infantino to resign following his attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup. The move has created a divide among FIFA member nations.

Mexico and Argentina have expressed their support for Infantino despite the controversy, demonstrating disagreement among national football associations over the proposed commercialization of the tournament.

cards.headline: Student describes fleeing Thai school shooting
cards.teaser: A pupil said she was standing in front of her teacher when the educator was shot during an attack that killed five teachers.
cards.body:
A 14-year-old student killed his grandparents before opening fire at his school on the outskirts of Bangkok on Friday morning. The teenager shot five people dead at the school and wounded 22 others, nine of whom were in critical condition, according to Thai health officials. Police said the suspect then took his own life.

The attack has highlighted ongoing concerns about gun violence in Thailand. A student who witnessed the shooting described standing directly in front of her teacher when the teacher was shot, and said she had to climb over a school fence to escape.

cards.teaser: A court ruled that Meta must pay $567 million in a child safety lawsuit, bringing total penalties in the case to $942 million.
cards.body:
Meta has been ordered to pay $567 million in the second phase of New Mexico's child safety case, bringing total fines to $942 million. A Santa Fe district court ruled that Meta's platforms are a "significant contributing cause" of harm to teenagers' mental health.

The ruling concludes a landmark trial where a jury found Meta knowingly harmed children's mental health and concealed information about child sexual exploitation on its platforms. cards.headline: July Jobs Report Expected to Show Nearly 100,000 Positions Added
cards.teaser: The monthly employment report is anticipated to reveal steady but modest job growth, with analysts forecasting the economy added close to 100,000 jobs in July.
cards.body:
The Labor Department is releasing July employment data, with economists projecting roughly 100,000 new jobs were added during the month. The report is closely watched by investors evaluating labor market strength and potential Federal Reserve policy shifts.

Job growth is expected to remain modest compared to previous years, reflecting a cooling labor market from post-pandemic peaks. Young workers and unemployed job seekers are facing greater challenges in securing positions. Stock futures rose ahead of the report's release as markets awaited confirmation of employment trends.

cards.headline: Chinese Robotics Firm Unitree Prices IPO at $900 Million
cards.teaser: Unitree Robotics has set pricing for an initial public offering aimed at raising $900 million, testing investor appetite for humanoid robot technology.
cards.body:
Chinese robotics manufacturer Unitree Robotics has priced its initial public offering with a goal of raising approximately $900 million. The IPO represents a test of market interest in humanoid robotics, a technology sector that has generated significant attention but remains commercially unproven at scale.

Unitree specializes in humanoid robot development, creating machines designed to perform tasks in industrial and consumer settings. The company's public market debut comes as investors weigh the potential of automation technology against questions about near-term commercial viability and profitability. The robotics sector has attracted substantial venture capital investment, but few companies have demonstrated sustainable revenue models from humanoid robot sales.

cards.headline: Chinese Exports Continue Growing Despite International Trade Tensions
cards.teaser: China's factory output has sustained strong export performance even as trade tensions increase and domestic economic challenges persist.
cards.body:
Chinese manufacturers continue to find strong demand for exports despite growing international trade backlash and tariff measures. The export growth comes as China's domestic economy faces headwinds from weak consumer spending and an extended downturn in the property sector.

Factories have maintained production levels by targeting overseas markets, offsetting sluggish demand at home. The sustained export performance demonstrates the resilience of Chinese manufacturing despite increasing trade barriers imposed by the United States and other trading partners. Analysts note that Chinese producers have adapted to shifting trade conditions by seeking new markets and adjusting pricing strategies to maintain competitiveness.

cards.headline: Senate Delays Vote on Cryptocurrency Clarity Act Until After Summer Break
cards.teaser: The Senate will not vote on digital asset legislation before its recess, postponing consideration of regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies.
cards.body:
The Senate has decided not to vote on the cryptocurrency Clarity Act before members leave for summer break, delaying consideration of proposed digital asset regulations. The legislation aims to establish a regulatory framework for cryptocurrency markets and clarify oversight responsibilities among federal agencies.

The delay extends uncertainty for cryptocurrency companies and investors seeking clear federal rules governing digital assets. Banking Committee leadership has called for Senate action on the bill, highlighting momentum in digital asset markets, but scheduling conflicts and disagreements over provisions have prevented floor consideration. The crypto industry has actively lobbied for passage, though some lawmakers and advocacy groups have raised concerns about specific elements of the proposed framework.

hero.headline: Astronomers capture highest-resolution image of Sun's surface
hero.body:
Astronomers using the NSF Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii have obtained the most detailed images ever recorded of the Sun's surface, revealing swirling structures and golden bands that illuminate previously unknown plasma processes. The breakthrough observations identified Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities across magnetically active regions near sunspots, a finding that may help solve one of solar physics' greatest mysteries.

The Inouye telescope, positioned near the summit of Haleakalā volcano on the island of Maui, captured features smaller than 20 kilometers across. These images represent the telescope operating at its maximum capability, surpassing previous observations that detected details of only 30 kilometers. "These are the highest spatial resolution images of the solar surface ever acquired," said Dr. Friedrich Wöger, a senior scientist at the National Solar Observatory, which operates the facility.

Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities form when fast-moving plasma slides past slower-moving fluid, creating shear forces at the interface. This generates small disturbances that develop into spiraling vortices resembling breaking waves. While scientists have previously observed these instabilities in Earth's oceans and lakes, as well as in the atmospheres of Jupiter and Saturn, this marks the first confirmed detection on the Sun.

"This is something we have never seen before in any solar observations," said Dr. David Kuridze, an astronomer involved in the research. The whirlpool-like structures visible in the images provide crucial insight into solar dynamics and energy transfer.

The discovery has significant implications for understanding the Sun's corona, the star's outer atmosphere that reaches temperatures of millions of degrees while the surface remains at approximately 6,000 degrees Celsius. Scientists have long puzzled over this temperature paradox. The swirling vortices may explain how magnetic field lines become twisted and braided, a process that releases energy and heats the corona.

"This could solve this biggest mystery of the last half a century for solar physics and astrophysics," Kuridze said. When Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities occur in the system, energy cascades into smaller scales before dissipating as heat, potentially accounting for the corona's extreme temperatures.

The research also advances understanding of explosive solar events, including solar flares, jets, and coronal mass ejections. These phenomena are powered by extreme, fluctuating magnetic fields generated by moving hot, charged plasma, though the underlying physics remains incompletely understood. By identifying the mechanisms that create braided magnetic field lines, scientists gain insight into what triggers these powerful explosions that can disrupt power grids, satellites, GPS systems, and communications on Earth.

The findings were published in the journal Nature, representing a major step forward in solar research and demonstrating the Inouye telescope's potential for future discoveries.

cards.headline: NASA extends Voyager 2 science mission with power management adjustment
cards.teaser: Engineers used a procedure they called the Big Bang to squeeze another year of power from the probe traveling in interstellar space.
cards.body:
NASA engineers have extended the Voyager 2 spacecraft's science mission by at least one year through a power management procedure. The team implemented what they informally termed a Big Bang maneuver to reconfigure the probe's power systems, allowing continued operation of its scientific instruments despite declining power reserves.

Voyager 2, launched in 1977, is currently operating in interstellar space beyond the influence of the Sun's magnetic field. The spacecraft's plutonium power source naturally degrades over time, forcing mission controllers to make difficult decisions about which systems to keep active. The new power adjustment allows Voyager 2 to maintain its science operations through at least 2027. Engineers are now evaluating whether a similar approach could work for Voyager 1, the probe's twin spacecraft.

cards.headline: OpenAI expands ChatGPT access with upgrades for free and paid users
cards.teaser: The company improved its GPT-5.6 Sol model in ChatGPT and removed text limits for free accounts.
cards.body:
OpenAI is removing message limits for ChatGPT's free and Go tier users, allowing unlimited text conversations starting next week. Previously, these users faced rate limits that restricted how many text chats they could have within certain timeframes.

The company is also improving the GPT-5.6 Sol model for ChatGPT and expanding free-tier access to the GPT-5.6 Luna model. Paid subscribers will benefit from enhancements to GPT-5.6 Sol, though the model's capabilities remain consistent across platforms.

cards.headline: OpenAI developing AI smart speaker priced between $300 and $400
cards.teaser: The device, designed with input from Jony Ive, will reportedly be hockey puck-sized and function as a premium AI assistant.
cards.body:
OpenAI is developing a smart speaker priced over $300 in collaboration with designer Jony Ive. The battery-powered device is roughly hockey puck-sized with a doughnut shape and will launch in 2027. According to reports, it functions as a smart speaker without a display.

The premium pricing positions the device well above mainstream smart speakers from Amazon and Google. OpenAI's offering targets users seeking advanced AI capabilities rather than competing in the mass-market segment.

cards.headline: Total solar eclipse to cross Europe on August 12
cards.teaser: The eclipse will create a path of totality through Spain and other European locations, with some areas experiencing rare double darkness.
cards.body:
A total solar eclipse will cross Europe on August 12, 2026, marking the UK's largest solar eclipse since 1999. The path of totality will pass through parts of Spain and extend to the Channel Islands and the West Country in the UK, where viewing opportunities will be available.

One Spanish village along the eclipse path will experience an unusual phenomenon where darkness falls twice in one night. Those positioned within the path of totality will witness several minutes of complete daytime darkness as the Moon fully blocks the Sun—a rare event for mainland Europe in recent decades.

cards.headline: Splatoon Raiders receives patch update to version 1.1.1
cards.teaser: Nintendo released patch notes for the latest update to the game, which sold over half a million copies in its first week in Japan.
cards.body:
Nintendo has released version 1.1.1 of Splatoon Raiders, a patch update for the recently launched game. The update includes various fixes and adjustments detailed in official patch notes published by the company. Splatoon Raiders debuted at the top of French game sales charts following its late June release.

The game sold more than half a million copies during its first week of sales in Japan alone, demonstrating strong initial performance for the franchise spinoff. Nintendo held a dedicated Splatoon Raiders Direct presentation on June 30, 2026, to showcase the game's features before launch. The 1.1.1 update represents Nintendo's ongoing support for the title following its commercial success in multiple markets.

cards.headline: Analyst predicts iPhone 18 Pro could cost up to $300 more than current models
cards.teaser: Apple is reportedly planning pricing increases for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup while preparing for a September launch event.
cards.body:
An analyst forecast suggests the iPhone 18 Pro models could see price increases of up to $300 compared to current iPhone pricing. The prediction comes as Apple prepares for its traditional September iPhone launch, with the company conducting an employee lottery for retail staff to work the event. A leaked memo also referenced Apple's plans for both an iPhone 18 Pro and a potential iPhone Ultra model.

Apple has announced iPhone events in September for six consecutive years, establishing a predictable launch pattern for its flagship devices. Bloomberg reported that Apple is coordinating with retail employees in preparation for the product release. If the price increase predictions prove accurate, the iPhone 18 Pro would represent one of the largest year-over-year price jumps in the product line's history.

hero.headline: Norrie saves match point to defeat De Minaur at Canadian Open
hero.body:
Britain's Cameron Norrie staged a dramatic comeback to defeat world number seven Alex de Minaur at the Canadian Open in Montreal, saving a match point in the process.

Norrie's fighting display showcased his competitive spirit against one of the tour's most consistent performers this season. The British player found himself in a precarious position during the match but demonstrated the mental toughness required to turn the contest around at a critical moment.

The Canadian Open stands as a premier event on the ATP Tour calendar, drawing elite players from around the globe during the summer hard court season. The tournament in Montreal provides a significant test for competitors as they prepare for the later stages of the season.

De Minaur, ranked seventh in the world, appeared well positioned for victory before Norrie mounted his remarkable fightback. The Australian's high ranking and consistent performances on tour made the comeback particularly impressive. Norrie's ability to save the match point proved to be the turning point in the hard-fought encounter.

This victory holds considerable importance for Norrie's trajectory through the tournament. Defeating a top ten player provides valuable momentum as he progresses through the competition. The win also offers encouragement as Norrie looks to build confidence on North American hard courts ahead of the US Open, which follows later in the summer.

Norrie's performance demonstrated the variety in his game and his willingness to take risks when needed. Rather than adopting a passive approach, he committed to aggressive shot-making and forced himself into attacking positions throughout the match. This bold strategy ultimately paid dividends despite initially appearing to be failing against De Minaur's consistent play.

The match reflected the unpredictable nature of professional tennis, where match-ups between particular players can significantly influence outcomes. While rankings suggest one player should prevail, individual styles and tactical approaches can create opportunities for lower-ranked competitors to upset the odds.

Norrie will advance to face his next opponent as the tournament continues its progression toward the final stages. The Canadian Open serves as important preparation for the US Open, another major hard court event that takes place shortly after. Success at events like Montreal can provide players with the confidence and momentum needed to perform well at major championships.

The win over De Minaur adds to Norrie's growing body of work against elite opposition. As he continues through the tournament, each victory against top-ranked players strengthens his overall record and provides valuable experience in high-pressure situations. The manner of this comeback victory, saving a match point and recovering from a seemingly lost position, exemplifies the resilience and determination that characterises Norrie's approach to professional tennis.

cards.headline: Norway calls for Infantino resignation over World Cup stake sale plan
cards.teaser: The Norwegian Football Federation has called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign after he attempted to sell stakes in the World Cup.
cards.body:
The Norwegian Football Federation has called for FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign over his plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. However, Mexico and Argentina have publicly backed Infantino, revealing divisions among FIFA member associations on the issue.

The controversy has widened, with UEFA reiterating its threat to boycott FIFA competitions and expressing loss of confidence in Infantino's leadership. Fifpro, the global players' union, condemned what it described as "a profound abuse of presidential power," while South American confederation Conmebol criticized Infantino's "repeated unilateral actions taken without resorting to dialogue."

cards.headline: Atletico Madrid in talks to sign Tottenham captain Romero
cards.teaser: Atletico Madrid has opened talks with Tottenham over a potential move for club captain Cristian Romero, who is expected to leave this summer.
cards.body:
Tottenham and Atlético Madrid are in talks over a potential transfer for captain Cristian Romero. The Argentine defender has expressed his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season. Tottenham rejected an approach from Arsenal for the 27-year-old.

Atlético Madrid are understood to be Romero's preferred destination, with manager Diego Simeone's side prepared to match Inter's offer of around £35 million. Meanwhile, Tottenham are expected to agree a new five-year deal with defender Micky van de Ven.

cards.headline: Arsenal midfielder Lewis-Skelly seeks midfield role after left-back debut
cards.teaser: Teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly broke into Arsenal's first team at left-back but has always preferred playing in midfield.
cards.body:
Myles Lewis-Skelly made his Arsenal first-team debut in the left-back position, but midfield is where the teenager truly wants to play. His versatility enabled him to break into the squad in a defensive role.

Now Lewis-Skelly has the chance to push for minutes in his preferred central midfield position, where he will compete with Arsenal's established players for a regular starting spot.

cards.headline: Arsenal women target treble after adding seven new players
cards.teaser: Midfielder Mariona Caldentey says Arsenal, strengthened by seven new signings, are talking up their chances of winning the treble this season.
cards.body:
Arsenal midfielder Mariona Caldentey has embraced the pressure surrounding the club's treble ambitions this season. With seven new players added to strengthen the squad, the Spanish midfielder views the heightened expectations as something positive for the team.

Caldentey's comments reflect Arsenal's confidence in their reinforced roster as they pursue multiple trophies. The midfielder's willingness to embrace these demands suggests the squad is united in their pursuit of a historic treble win.

cards.headline: West Ham owner Sullivan expected to attend cup match despite safety concerns
cards.teaser: David Sullivan is expected to attend West Ham's EFL Cup match against Portsmouth despite being advised to stay away from home games.
cards.body:
West Ham owner David Sullivan is expected to attend Saturday's EFL Cup first-round match against Portsmouth at the London Stadium, despite receiving safety advice to avoid home matches at the ground.

Sullivan's decision to attend comes as the club prepares for the opening round of the cup competition.

cards.headline: Chelsea faces challenge cutting 41-player senior squad
cards.teaser: With 25 days remaining in the transfer window, Chelsea is working to reduce its 41-player senior squad.
cards.body:
Chelsea has 25 days to trim its 41-player senior squad before the transfer window closes. The club must facilitate multiple departures to reach a more sustainable squad size.

The Blues face the task of identifying which players will leave as the deadline approaches. Chelsea is actively working to move players out during the remaining transfer window period.

hero.headline: Indian Director Vishal Bhardwaj Developing Film on Tarun Tejpal Rape Case Following Conviction
hero.body:
Indian filmmaker Vishal Bhardwaj confirmed he is developing a film based on the Tarun Tejpal rape case, hours after the Bombay High Court overturned an earlier acquittal and convicted the former Tehelka editor of rape. The court sentenced Tejpal to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

Bhardwaj, known for his adaptations of Shakespeare including Maqbool, Omkara, and Haider, plans to structure the film in a Rashomon-style format. This approach typically presents the same events from multiple perspectives, allowing different characters to offer their own versions of what occurred. The director confirmed the project in a conversation with Variety.

The case involves Tejpal, who previously served as editor of the investigative magazine Tehelka. A Goa sessions court had initially acquitted him, but the Bombay High Court reversed that decision, finding him guilty of rape. The High Court then imposed a decade-long sentence of rigorous imprisonment, a term that typically involves mandatory labor alongside incarceration.

Bhardwaj has built a reputation for tackling complex and controversial subjects through cinema. His Shakespeare adaptations transported the playwright's works to contemporary Indian settings, addressing themes of power, violence, and corruption. The filmmaker's decision to take on the Tejpal case continues this pattern of engaging with challenging material that intersects law, media, and society.

The timing of the announcement, coming within hours of the High Court conviction, suggests Bhardwaj had been tracking the case through its legal progression. The Rashomon format he plans to employ could allow the film to explore the conflicting narratives and perspectives that often emerge in high-profile criminal cases, particularly those involving powerful media figures.

cards.headline: Luca Guadagnino to Receive Filmmaker Award at Venice Film Festival
cards.teaser: The Italian director will be honored at this year's Venice Film Festival while premiering his seven-hour documentary on Bernardo Bertolucci.
cards.body:
Luca Guadagnino will receive the Cartier Glory to the Filmmaker Award at this year's Venice Film Festival. The Italian director is being honored as a personality who has made a particularly original contribution to the contemporary film industry.

Guadagnino will premiere his seven-hour documentary Joie de Vivre at the festival. The film focuses on the life and work of Italian director Bernardo Bertolucci, who directed classics including Last Tango in Paris and The Last Emperor before his death in 2018.

cards.headline: Werner Herzog to Receive Donostia Award at San Sebastián Film Festival
cards.teaser: The German filmmaker will be honored at the festival's opening gala in September during its 74th edition.
cards.body:
Werner Herzog will receive the San Sebastián Film Festival's Donostia Award during its 74th edition in September. The German director will be honored at the Spanish festival's opening gala and will screen his latest film Bucking Fastard, following its world premiere at Venice Film Festival.

Herzog's career spans six decades of filmmaking. The prolific director has produced a wide-ranging body of work across documentary and narrative films, establishing himself as one of cinema's most distinctive voices.

cards.headline: Bella Thorne Directing, Writing, and Starring in Spring Breakers Sequel
cards.teaser: The former Disney star is taking on multiple roles in the upcoming sequel to Harmony Korine's 2012 cult film.
cards.body:
Bella Thorne revealed she is directing, writing, and starring in an upcoming sequel to Spring Breakers. The former Disney star is taking on all three roles for the follow-up to Harmony Korine's 2012 cult classic.

Variety announced the sequel and its cast in May 2025, which also includes Grace Van Dien from Stranger Things. Thorne described the project as being hers from start to finish. The original Spring Breakers starred Selena Gomez, Vanessa Hudgens, Ashley Benson, and James Franco in a story about college students on spring break who become involved with a drug dealer.

cards.headline: Danny DeVito-Produced Heist Comedy Drag Heads to Toronto Film Festival Market
cards.teaser: Blue Finch Films has acquired international sales rights for the film directed by Greg Yagolnitzer and Raviv Ullman.
cards.body:
Blue Finch Films has taken on international sales rights outside North America for the heist thriller comedy Drag. The UK sales and distribution company plans to launch the title at the market during the Toronto Film Festival.

Danny DeVito, Lucy DeVito, and Jake DeVito produced the film, which was directed by Greg Yagolnitzer and Raviv Ullman. Blue Finch Films will handle distribution and sales in territories outside North America at the Toronto market.

cards.headline: Brandon Flowers Releases Single Tigers Blood Ahead of New Album
cards.teaser: The Killers frontman will release his new album Thrasher later this month.
cards.body:
Brandon Flowers has released his new single "Tiger's Blood," an anthemic track that reflects on the past. The Killers frontman is gearing up to drop his upcoming album Thrasher later this month.

The album marks fresh solo material from Flowers, who is renowned as the lead vocalist and keyboardist of the rock band The Killers.

cards.headline: Thomas Heise's Final Documentary Premieres at Locarno Film Festival
cards.teaser: The late German filmmaker's final work arrives at the festival as both a portrait and a completion of an unfinished project.
cards.body:
Thomas Heise's final film, übergang, will premiere in the out of competition section at the Locarno Film Festival. The documentary arrives as both a portrait of one of Germany's most influential documentary filmmakers and the completion of a project left unfinished by his death.

The film traces Heise's life through newly shot footage, archival material, and photographs. It reflects on themes of time and transience, serving as a final statement from the German director whose work shaped documentary filmmaking in his country.

hero.headline: Murkowski opposes Blanche for attorney general, threatening confirmation
hero.body:
Sen. Lisa Murkowski announced Friday she will vote against Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general, putting his confirmation in serious jeopardy. The Alaska Republican becomes the second GOP senator to publicly oppose the nominee, joining Sen. Susan Collins of Maine.

Murkowski said in a Friday morning post on social media that the country needs an attorney general who will check the worst impulses of the administration. She stated she lacks confidence that Blanche would fulfill that role if confirmed.

The opposition from both senators is significant because Republicans control the Senate with only a narrow margin. Blanche can afford to lose just two Republican votes, assuming all Democrats vote against him and Sen. Mitch McConnell remains absent. With Murkowski and Collins both opposed, the nomination faces substantial obstacles.

Louisiana Sen. Bill Cassidy remains undecided on the nomination, adding uncertainty to Blanche's path forward.

However, the source material indicates that Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis, who were previously holding out on their support, announced they would advance Blanche's nomination after reaching what they called a "successful negotiation of a legally enforceable document." This agreement addressed concerns about provisions in a Trump settlement with the Internal Revenue Service.

Specifically, the document formally ends a planned 1.8 billion dollar fund referred to as an "anti-weaponization fund." The agreement also clarifies that Trump and his family will not receive indefinite protection from audits of future tax filings. Both the fund and the scope of Trump's immunity from audits had become dealbreakers for Cornyn and Tillis.

"We are pleased that the Department of Justice has issued a formal order terminating the anti-weaponization fund," Cornyn and Tillis said in a joint statement. They added that the department acknowledged in a binding written order that the audit settlement is limited to the plaintiffs in the original lawsuit and does not extend to other parties.

The attorney general position oversees the Justice Department and serves as the nation's chief law enforcement officer. The role includes supervising federal prosecutors and providing legal counsel to the executive branch.

Blanche, who is already serving as acting attorney general, is scheduled to face a Senate judiciary committee vote on his permanent confirmation.

The Senate judiciary committee is due to vote on whether to approve the nomination and send it to the wider Senate for a vote. The timing of the vote had not yet been scheduled at the time the original article was written, though the source material indicates it would occur soon after the agreement was reached.

cards.headline: Trump approval rating drops as war, tariffs weigh on support
cards.teaser: President Trump's approval rating has fallen to the 30s as an ongoing war in Iran and economic concerns strain public support.
cards.body:
President Trump's approval rating has dropped into the 30s as a war in Iran and tariff policies weigh on public sentiment. Longtime insiders express concern that the president remains focused on the war, tariffs, and monument construction despite their unpopularity in polls.

The three issues consume much of Trump's time and attention heading into the midterm elections. Republicans face the challenge of campaigning while these topics dominate the political landscape, with little indication that public opinion will shift in their favor before November.

cards.headline: Republicans plan midterm convention focused on Democratic left
cards.teaser: The GOP will use its first midterm convention next month to argue Democrats have become captive to their activist left wing.
cards.body:
Republicans plan to hold their first-ever midterm convention in Dallas next month, where they will focus on attacking Democrats' progressive wing. The party intends to present a prime-time case against socialism and Democratic policies.

The strategy reflects Republican efforts to shift voter attention away from the president's approval ratings, which remain in the 30s. By centering the midterm message on opposition policies rather than the administration's record, Republicans aim to make Democrats the primary concern for voters in November's elections.

cards.headline: Harassment allegations complicate Republican midterm messaging
cards.teaser: Multiple abuse and harassment allegations involving GOP lawmakers threaten to overshadow the party's midterm campaign message.
cards.body:
House Republicans are dealing with allegations of abuse or harassment involving several members months before the midterm elections. Domestic abuse allegations against Rep. Max Miller of Ohio and scrutiny of Reps. Cory Mills of Florida and Chuck Edwards of North Carolina have emerged as the party prepares its campaign strategy.

The allegations present a messaging challenge for Republicans as they seek to focus voter attention on policy issues ahead of November. Party leaders must address the controversies while attempting to maintain their campaign narrative going into the final months before the election.

cards.headline: States implement uneven protections against AI election deepfakes
cards.teaser: Twenty-nine states have laws addressing AI-generated election content, creating varied protections across the country ahead of the midterms.
cards.body:
Twenty-nine states have enacted laws governing AI deepfakes in elections, while California and Hawaii have had their laws blocked by courts. The patchwork of regulations means voters will experience different levels of protection from AI-generated political content heading into Election Day.

AI-generated attack ads and campaign materials have become widespread in the current midterm cycle, with candidates across the political spectrum using the technology. The lack of uniform federal standards leaves regulation to individual states, resulting in inconsistent protections for voters nationwide.

cards.headline: Rubio intensifies economic pressure on Cuba
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is conducting what he describes as an unprecedented economic campaign against Cuba's communist government.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters the administration is waging an economic war on Cuba and plans to increase pressure on the island's leaders. Rubio said the strategy aims to eliminate any relief mechanisms for the Cuban government.

Cuba's economy faces strain from U.S. sanctions and internal management issues. President Trump has not ruled out military action against the island nation, which is located 90 miles from U.S. shores. The economic pressure campaign represents an escalation in U.S. policy toward its longtime adversary.

cards.headline: Tariff refunds boost quarterly earnings for major corporations
cards.teaser: Major U.S. companies reported significant boosts to quarterly earnings from Trump administration tariff refunds totaling $100 billion.
cards.body:
The Trump administration returned the bulk of $100 billion in tariff refunds during the latest quarter, providing earnings boosts to major corporations. Amazon received $600 million in refunds, while Apple said the returns added $0.11 per share to diluted earnings.

PepsiCo also reported tariff refunds as a factor in its quarterly results. The refunds have appeared across multiple corporate earnings reports as companies disclose the financial impact of the returned payments. The timing of the refunds coincided with the quarterly reporting period for many large U.S. firms.
